purpose: Vetted transcription of NAPIC official commercial property indicators (PBO, Shopping Complex, Serviced Apartment overhang, SOHO overhang, Shops) for use on myproperty.investmquest.com. Produced 2026-08-12 as v1-draft2 (shops deep-dive: national annual overhang series 2017-2025, by-state overhang 2021-2026, shop transactions, and the Q1 2026 shop/SOHO/SA supply pipeline); promoted to v1 same day after human spot-check of the source XLS files. See VERIFICATION.md section 'Shops deep-dive (v1-draft2)' for the original transcription log. Extended same day to v2-draft with price_band_breakdown_q1_2026 (price-band x storey-type split of the Q1 2026 shop/SOHO/SA unsold figures already anchored in v1, Table 8 of the same source file); schema left at v2 of this addition before promotion to v2. Extended same day with price_band_breakdown_q1_2026 (price bands x 5 geos x shop/SOHO/SA + national storey-type split); promoted to v2 after human spot-check of Table 8 band cells.
discipline: Every value is transcribed from an official NAPIC file (quarterly Excel tables downloaded from napic.jpph.gov.my, or a printed data table embedded under a chart in an official NAPIC Annual/Half-Year Property Market Report PDF). Nothing is interpolated, estimated, smoothed, or sourced from any second-hand republication. Missing = null. Any derived value (e.g. unit conversion, percentage share) is flagged with a 'basis' field naming the raw figures it was derived from. notes.pboScope: IMPORTANT: the quarterly CBSA table (Jadual Penghunian dan Ketersediaan Ruang Bangunan Perdagangan) is explicitly titled '... BANGUNAN PEJABAT BINAAN KHAS (MILIK SWASTA) ...' i.e. PURPOSE-BUILT OFFICE, PRIVATELY-OWNED ONLY. It does NOT include government-owned office buildings. The Annual Property Market Report's PBO chart is explicitly titled 'Private & Government' (combined). These are two different scopes of the same NAPIC PBO series and must not be treated as interchangeable. This resolves what the task brief flagged as a 72% vs 78% conflict in second-hand sources — see VERIFICATION.md.
notes.shoppingComplexVsCentre: The CBSA file (and the underlying NAPIC classification) has two distinct retail tables: Table 2 'Kompleks Perniagaan / Shopping Complex' and Table 3 'Pusat Beli-Belah / Shopping Centre'. The task asked for 'Shopping Complex', which is Table 2 (larger national space than Table 3). Table 3 was read but is not reported in this draft since it is a narrower/different category, not a subtotal of Table 2. If 'Shopping Centre' is later found to be a required category, TABLE 3 data was already captured in the session (national MALAYSIA Q1 2026: 13,205.28 '000 s.m. existing, 10,155.06 '000 s.m. occupied, 76.90% occupancy, 499 buildings) and can be added on request.
notes.unitConversion: NAPIC reports commercial building space in '000 square metres (s.m.). Where this draft states a sqft-equivalent for cross-checking against a second-hand sqft figure, the conversion constant used is 1 sqm = 10.7639 sqft, and the derived sqft value is explicitly flagged basis='derived_unit_conversion'. All primary transcribed values are stored in the NAPIC native unit (sqm) or units (dwelling count), never pre-converted.
notes.shopOverhangExists: The task brief hypothesised NAPIC has no overhang/unsold indicator for shops. This is INCORRECT and is corrected here: Jadual Status Pasaran Harta Tanah Table 8 explicitly covers 'KEDAI' (Shop) alongside SOHO and Serviced Apartment, with an unsold-completed unit count and RM value, by state and price range. Shop overhang IS a published NAPIC indicator; it was simply absent from the specific report cited as the source for that claim in prior research. See VERIFICATION.md.
notes.reviewCorrections_2026_08_12: Human review of the source XLS files on 2026-08-12 found three source-citation offsets in the working draft (v1-draft2). In every case the underlying transcribed values were confirmed correct against the raw files — only the row/location metadata was mislabeled. (1) Table 8 state-block rows: the actual layout is TOTAL label row = Unit Launched, +1 row = Unsold Units, +2 rows = Value RM million — e.g. Malaysia's TOTAL block is r42/r43/r44, not 'r41-43' as the draft stated; the same +1 shift applies to every Table 8 row citation carried over from the draft (WP KL r80-82, WP Putrajaya r118-120, Selangor r194-196, Johor r232-234, Pulau Pinang r270-272), and to the by_state_annual row-offset formula (corrected below from start+34/35/36 to start+35/36/37). (2)-(3) shop_overhang_and_stock.existing_stock_q1_2026's source location was corrected: the MALAYSIA total row is TABLE 1 r27 (not r26 as drafted), and the state rows (WP KL etc.) are read from TABLE 2 r20 (not 'TABLE 1, state rows starting r9' as drafted). No numeric value in this file was changed as a result of this review; only source/row annotations were corrected.

price_and_rental_narrative_2025.note: NAPIC's annual report does not carry a shop price INDEX or average-price table; price/rental commentary is qualitative, citing specific schemes as illustrative examples. Captured here as narrative context only, not a structured time series - do not treat any of these as a market-wide average.
price_examples: WP Kuala Lumpur: double-storey shops in Lucky Garden, Bandar Manjalara, and Taman Shamelin Perkasa recorded price increases of 17%, 12.8%, and 14.7% respectively.
Selangor, Johor and Pulau Pinang: double- and three-storey shop market prices showed marginal increases across several districts; some other schemes showed a downward trend, mostly less than 10%.
rental_examples: WP Kuala Lumpur: highest rentals nationally, up to RM30,000/month at Changkat Bukit Bintang; Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman RM17,000-RM34,000/month; Bangsar Baru RM15,000-RM19,000/month.
Selangor: upward rental movement in Petaling and Hulu Langat districts; Bandar Setia Alam highest at RM7,000-RM8,500/month.
Johor Bahru: Jalan Tun Abdul Razak rental +7.7% to RM3,000-RM4,000/month; Jalan Wong Ah Fook highest in the district at RM7,500-RM9,500/month.
Pulau Pinang: Jalan Perak (Timur Laut district) rental +8.4% to RM3,500-RM4,700/month; Seberang Perai Tengah/Utara/Selatan rentals up 2.2%-15.2%.

price_band_breakdown_q1_2026.definition: Unsold Completed Units and Value (RM million), by state, category (Shop total / SOHO / Serviced Apartment) and price range, transcribed cell-by-cell from Table 8 of the Q1 2026 Jadual Status Pasaran Harta Tanah file (same table already used elsewhere in this file for the category TOTALs). 'Unit Launched' row was read but is not transcribed here (not requested).

source.row_layout: Each state block is 38 rows: label row, then 11 price bands x 3 rows (Unit Launched / Unsold Units / Value RM Million), then a 3-row TOTAL block (same 3-row pattern), then 1 blank row. Block start rows (0-indexed): MALAYSIA=7, W.P. KUALA LUMPUR=45, SELANGOR=159, JOHOR=197, PULAU PINANG=235. Within a block, band i (0-indexed, i=0..10) occupies rows [start+1+3i, start+2+3i, start+3+3i] = [Unit Launched, Unsold Units, Value]; TOTAL occupies rows [start+34, start+35, start+36]. Columns: c2-c10=shop by storey/type (1-1.5 storey, 2-2.5 storey, 3-3.5 storey, 4-4.5 storey, 5-5.5 storey, Above 5.5 storey, Semi Detached, Detached, Stratified), c11=SHOP Total, c13=SOHO, c14=Serviced Apartment.

national.interpretation_note: In the two intervals ending Q3 and Q4 2025, new supply added exceeded net absorption (136.07 > 69.52; 96.55 > 74.32), so the national occupancy rate was flat-to-declining even though absorption itself was positive. In the Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026 interval, net absorption (126.85) exceeded new supply (61.36) for the first time in this series, and available space fell in absolute terms (5220.91 -> 5155.42 '000 sm) - the +0.44pp occupancy gain in that quarter is attributable to demand outpacing supply, not to a shrinking denominator alone. This is a derived read of four data points, not a trend call; a fifth quarter (Q2 2026) would be needed to confirm continuation.

wp_kuala_lumpur.note: Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026: total existing space FELL 9662.34 -> 9633.72 ('000 sm, -28.62) while occupied space rose (+69.01) - the +0.93pp occupancy gain this quarter reflects both real absorption and a stock reduction (building reclassification, demolition, or data revision - not distinguished by this source), not absorption alone.

selangor.note: Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026: occupied space FELL (3169.50 -> 3142.33, -27.17 '000 sm) even as total stock also fell (-18.31) - occupancy dropped 71.79% -> 71.47%, the only one of the four states/national tracked here where the most recent quarter shows genuine net negative absorption, not just a supply effect.

johor.note: Occupied space FELL Q1->Q3 2025 (557.78 -> 531.03, two quarters combined) even as stock grew - a genuine demand-side deterioration, not a supply dilution effect. Occupancy has since stabilised around 55% for three straight readings (54.15% / 55.11% / 55.15%), consistent with the by_state_2025_private_and_government figure already in this file (66.4%, a different Private+Government scope, see notes.pboScope) sitting well above this private-only reading.

pulau_pinang.note: Q3 2025 -> Q4 2025: total stock jumped +33.72 '000 sm (roughly 4.6% of the Q3 base, a single quarter) while occupied space fell slightly (-4.43) - occupancy dropped sharply, 80.38% -> 76.22% (-4.16pp), a clean case of a supply-driven dilution event rather than a demand shock. Partial recovery followed, +1.09pp to 77.31% by Q1 2026.

capital_markets_2025.definition: Named-transaction sales data from Laporan Pasaran Harta Tanah 2025 (Annual Property Market Report), Overview chapter, Table 2 (Shopping Complex) and Table 4 (Purpose-Built Office). These are 'Summary of Major Sales' tables - a curated list of the largest/most notable deals NAPIC's overview chapter chose to name, not an exhaustive transaction register (see reconciliation notes below).

narrative_total.text_en: In 2025, market activity recorded several office building transactions with an accumulated value exceeded RM2.08 billion.

office_table4_purpose_built_office.reconciliation_note: The 20 rows printed in Table 4 sum to RM1,419,417,233 (~RM1.42bn) - well short of the narrative's 'exceeded RM2.08 billion'. Table 4 is therefore explicitly a partial/illustrative listing, not the full basis for the RM2.08bn figure; the gap (~RM660m) is in deals NAPIC did not itemise by name. Do not present Table 4's row-sum as if it equals or explains the RM2.08bn headline - the two are separate, both-official numbers with a stated gap.
office_table4_purpose_built_office.kl_rows_reference: The 9 WP Kuala Lumpur rows (Menara CIMB RM680.0m 2025; Wisma Technip RM135.0m 2025; Menara Southern Bank RM91.3m 2025; Widad Business Group RM41.5m 2025; KSK Building RM33.0m 2025; Southbank Boutique Office - Block 6 RM29.5m 2025; Menara Affin RM100.0m 2024; SB-10 The Bouleverd Signature Offices Mid Valley City RM36.76m 2024; SB-09 The Bouleverd Signature Offices Mid Valley City RM23.24m 2024) are transcribed in data/napic-kl-commercial.json, not duplicated here - see that file for the KL-specific presentation.

office_table4_purpose_built_office.state_size_gap_note: Every one of the 11 non-KL office rows is below RM56 million; the largest, Basis Bay in Cyberjaya (RM55.6m) and Menara Apex in Kajang (RM55.0m), are both Selangor deals and both still smaller than 6 of the 9 KL rows. The single largest KL row alone (Menara CIMB, RM680.0m) exceeds the combined sum of all 11 non-KL rows (RM249.07m). This is a magnitude gap consistent with - not proof of, given Table 4 is a curated 'major sales' list, not a census - the scale difference between KL's institutional office market and every other state's.

narrative_total.text_en: The reviewed year recorded several shopping complex transactions with an accumulative worth of RM3.48 billion; mostly of the transactions were in Selangor, WP Kuala Lumpur, Johor, Pahang, Perak and only one in Sabah.

historical_shop_transactions_annual.task: Extend transactions.shops_national_annual_series (currently 2021-2025 only) further back in time.
historical_shop_transactions_annual.result: GAP - no reliable shop-specific transaction volume/value series was found before 2021 in any NAPIC publication available in this archive.
what_was_checked: AnnualReport2012.txt through AnnualReport2017.txt: contain PBO, Shopping Complex, and shop-overhang appendix tables (used above), but NO shop-specific transaction volume/value table. The transaction tables in these older reports are aggregated at 'commercial' (all sub-types combined) or 'shop-office/shoplot' categories that do not isolate 'shop' the way the 2025 Annual Report's Chart 24/25 does.

The 2021 Annual Report's transaction chapter (checked in an earlier phase of this same research effort, per existing committed notes) likewise only has an all-commercial aggregate chart (referred to there as 'Chart 13/14'-style), not a shop-specific one.

The archive's earlier Annual Report vintages (2012-2017) were searched specifically for a 'Jadual'-numbered raw transaction table broken out by property sub-type (shop vs shop-office vs SoHo vs purpose-built office) at the national level; none was found — transaction tables in this vintage range are organised by state and by broad category (residential/commercial/industrial/agricultural/development land), not by commercial sub-type.
historical_shop_transactions_annual.conclusion: Item 4 of the task (shop annual transaction volume/value further back than 2021) could not be extended with a primary NAPIC transcription. Compounding the 2021-2025 series backwards using narrative YoY percentages from earlier reports was considered and deliberately rejected, per this task's discipline against using derived/second-hand numbers as primary data. The existing 2021-2025 committed series (transactions.shops_national_annual_series) remains the full extent of what is directly transcribable from NAPIC's own tables in this archive.
historical_shop_transactions_annual.not_used_as_primary: Various narrative percentage-change statements referencing shop/shoplot transactions exist in the prose sections of the 2012-2017 reports (e.g. YoY % change commentary), but these were not entered here because they are narrative claims about YoY change, not a table of absolute annual volume/value figures, and back-solving absolute figures from a chain of percentages would compound rounding error across 5+ years - inconsistent with the append-only/no-second-hand-numbers discipline for this file.
